sections.label: DPT services licensing scope
sections.summary: The Bill expands DPT services in the PS Act to three activities and requires entities providing them as a business in Singapore to be licensed by MAS.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (on behalf of the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: In regulating these virtual assets service providers, the Bill will expand the scope of DPT services in the PS Act to include the following three activities: one, facilitating the transmission of DPTs from one account to another; two, custodial services for DPTs; and three, facilitating the exchange of DPTs where the service provider does not come into possession of the moneys or DPTs involved.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (on behalf of the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: The Bill will require an entity that provides any of these services as a business in Singapore to be licensed and subject to rules and regulations set by MAS in subsidiary legislation.

sections.label: Cross-border money transfer definition
sections.summary: The Bill broadens the cross-border money transfer service definition to include transfers between persons in different jurisdictions where the provider does not accept money in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (on behalf of the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: The Bill will broaden the definition of cross-border money transfer service to include facilitating transfers of money between persons in different jurisdictions where money is not accepted or received by the service provider in Singapore.

sections.label: MAS user protection measures
sections.summary: The Bill enables MAS to impose user protection measures on DPT service providers when necessary, such as segregating customer assets from its own.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (on behalf of the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: The Bill will enable MAS to impose user protection measures on DPT service providers when necessary.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (on behalf of the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: This could include, for example, requiring a DPT service provider to segregate customer assets from its own assets.

sections.label: Duty of care all persons
sections.summary: The Bill clarifies the general duty of care on information provided to MAS applies to all persons, not only individuals.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (on behalf of the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: Thirdly, the PS Act today requires an individual to use reasonable care to ensure that any information he or she provides to MAS under the PS Act is not false or misleading in any material particular.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (on behalf of the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: The Bill will clarify that this general duty of care applies to all persons, whether or not the person is an individual.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The list will include those providing services centered on Digital Payment Token (DPT) and those facilitating cross-border money transfers where the money does not pass through Singapore.

sections.label: Customer due diligence DPT providers
sections.summary: MAS stated the Bill obligates DPT service providers to conduct customer due diligence against money laundering and terrorism financing, leaving no anonymous cryptocurrency trading short of peer-to-peer.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In its public consultation, MAS made clear that this Bill will obligate DPT service providers to conduct customer due diligence to guard against money laundering and terrorism financing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: These requirements mean that short of peer-to-peer trading, there is no way to trade cryptocurrencies in Singapore anonymously.

sections.label: Anonymised financial transactions policy stance
sections.summary: The question asks whether MAS has reached a final policy stance on providing space for anonymised financial transactions in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Having sought the views of the public and the industry, can the Minister share whether MAS has reached a final policy stance on whether it envisions providing any space for anonymised financial transactions in Singapore?

sections.label: Sharing feedback on suspicious transaction reports
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Government will share more detailed feedback with financial institutions that file suspicious transaction reports, including on illegal wildlife trade.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Will the Government consider sharing feedback with greater details when financial institutions do provide suspicious transaction reports, including on the illegal wildlife trade?

sections.label: Singapore ICOs and blockchain companies
sections.summary: The passage states that in 2018 Singapore was the second most popular country for ICOs, and that 234 blockchain companies operated there as of November 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In 2018, Singapore was the second most popular country in the world for ICOs, and as of November 2020, 234 blockchain companies were operating in Singapore.

sections.label: Guidance needed on DPT service providers
sections.summary: The passage states the expanded DPT service provider definition will capture more activities, but MAS guidance is needed on control, inducing and arranging.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The expanded definition of DPT service provider will capture more activities, but more guidance is needed from MAS as to what constitutes certain activities such as, control, inducing and arranging.

sections.label: PSA amendment and FATF standards
sections.summary: The passage says amending the Payment Services Act to meet FATF standards may be onerous for payment service providers with different or lower risk levels.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: While it is laudable that the Payment Services Act or PSA is amended to greater meet the Financial Action Task Force or FATF standards, it maybe onerous for certain payment service providers to meet the same licensing requirement despite posting different or lower levels of risk.

sections.label: Token custody and payment service licence
sections.summary: The passage states companies with a capital markets licence and token custody service must still hold a payment service licence, with an exception for incidental token functions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Current companies who one, have a capital markets licence, and two, provide a token custody service must still hold a payment service licence with an exception available, if a token's function is merely incidental to the business of that payment service provider.

sections.label: MAS powers over DPT service providers
sections.summary: The passage states the amendment Bill gives MAS powers to impose user protection measures on certain DPT service providers and additional measures via subsidiary legislation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The amendment Bill before us provides additional powers to the MAS to, firstly, impose user protection measures on certain DPT service providers; and secondly, impose additional measures on any DPT service provider or class of DPT service providers by way of subsidiary legislation.

sections.label: Payment licence applicant numbers
sections.summary: 366 firms applied for exemption from holding a licence under the PSA, and 439 firms currently hold the payment licence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: These companies also struggle to account to their investors or shareholders and their future plans and as a result, go into hibernation or may leave the country.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: There are 366 firms who applied for exemption from holding a licence under the PSA for specific payment services for a specified period while waiting for their licence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: For example, DPT marketers and custodian service providers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: There are 439 firms who currently hold the payment licence.

sections.label: MAS payment Regulatory Evaluation Programme
sections.summary: MAS launched the payment Regulatory Evaluation Programme in 2019 to assist payment service providers, but it ceases in January 2021 and lacks targeted support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Firms coming through this programme in the UK are being authorised on average 40% faster than the standard applicant.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I note that the MAS launch the payment Regulatory Evaluation Programme in 2019, meant to assist payment service providers and seeking legal advice from registered Singapore law practises relating to the PSA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This entails a sample questionnaire for potential applicants to approach law firms with, and the list of legal practitioners who can provide advice in relation to the PSA, but it does not provide targeted support like what is being done in the UK.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Furthermore, this programme will cease in January 2021, one year after the PSA has come into force and the transitional period has ended; and (c) I would like to ask if the MAS can provide high-level guidance on the criteria determining approval or rejection of a licence.

sections.label: Amendment shows technological obsolescence
sections.summary: An amendment needed one year after enactment shows how quickly technological developments render legislation obsolete.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The very fact that an amendment is needed so soon just one year after the enactment of the original Act demonstrates the speed by which technological developments can render even the best laid legislation rapidly obsolete or, at the very least, struggling to catch up.

sections.label: Longer grace period for moneychangers
sections.summary: MAS plans a six-month exemption for newly regulated entities, and the speaker asks about a longer grace period for moneychangers.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Accordingly, while MAS has plans to grant a six-month exemption for newly regulated entities under this amendment Bill, I wonder if there is scope for an even longer phased-in grace period applying only to moneychangers in light of their extremely challenging business climate at the moment.

sections.label: All licensees replaces major licensees
sections.summary: By replacing the term major with all licensees, the language no longer automatically precludes small players.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Even so, by no longer limiting the Act's applicability with the term "major" to now include "all licensees", the language no longer automatically precludes small players.

sections.label: Easier conditions for e-Sing dollars
sections.summary: The speaker suggests it would seem fair to exercise easier regulatory conditions for institutions transacting in e-Sing dollars.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: If so, then it would seem fair to exercise somewhat easier regulatory conditions for institutions transacting in e-Sing dollars.

sections.label: Payment Services Amendment Bill licensing
sections.summary: The Payment Services (Amendment) Bill requires payment service entities, including DPT services, to be licensed and meet money laundering and terrorism financing risk standards.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: As such, the Payment Services (Amendment) Bill and the requirement for entities carrying on a business of providing payment services in Singapore, including a DPT service, to be licensed and meet standards for mitigation of risks relating to money laundering and terrorism financing are steps in the right direction to develop the financial services industry and to encourage digital innovation in the fintech space with the necessary safeguards.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The Payment Services (Amendment) Bill further regulates activities across a wider range of digital payment services as well as expands the definition of "digital payment token services" to regulate activities of virtual asset service providers like digital exchanges, cryptocurrency firms and e-wallet services.

sections.label: Seniors and digital payment tokens
sections.summary: The Bill expands digital payment token services to include marketing, and safeguards are proposed for marketing to seniors.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: They represent a large untapped market for digital payment token service providers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Thus, the Payment Services (Amendment) Bill, which expands the definition of "digital payment token services" to include marketing activities of the licensee is a welcome one to ensure that the marketing to these seniors, which is a big untapped market, would be done responsibly.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I propose to include safeguards when soliciting the seniors to subscribe to and transact in payment services using digital payment tokens as the underlying mechanics are complex and the risks may not be fully understood or accepted.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Some of the safeguards could be in the form of: (a) ensuring that, as part of the marketing and know-your-customer process, MAS to require providers to explicitly highlight the risks involved, especially with digital payment tokens; (b) ensuring that seniors must have gone through a risk assessment by the providers on the understanding of digital payment tokens; (c) lastly, ensuring that providers have algorithms to identify suspicious transactions prior to processing and delaying these suspicious transactions to enable customers, especially the seniors, to have time to think through.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: This will provide transactional level safeguards that will reduce scams and fraud targeting at the seniors.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The Payment Services (Amendment) Bill and the additional requirements to be imposed are steps that will enable Singapore to remain competitive and attractive to the best talents to build the next breakthrough in digital banking and digital payment token services.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: But as a society, we must also take steps to ensure that everyone, including the seniors, can participate and benefit from this transformation.

sections.label: KuCoin hack and Grab glitches
sections.summary: KuCoin reportedly had US$280 million in digital coins stolen in September 2020, and Grab had four technology glitches over two years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: KuCoin made global headlines with a reported US$280 million digital coins stolen from a cyber hack recently in September 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Similarly, Bloomberg, on 13 September 2020, reported that Grab, our payments' unicorn, had four repeated technology glitches over two years in technology applications relating to exposure of private data.

sections.label: Three areas for e-payment firms
sections.summary: Three areas are proposed for the Minister's consideration to encourage e-payment firms without too much regulatory burden, as practised in Hong Kong.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Given this, there are three areas that I would like to propose for the Minister's consideration to encourage firms in the e-payment space to undertake the necessary focus without too much regulatory burden.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: This is already being practised in other major financial centres, such as Hong Kong, where its monetary authority has put in place its cyber resilience assessment framework to mitigate hacks, fraud and data leakage risks.

sections.label: Educating and protecting customers
sections.summary: Firms should devote adequate efforts and resources to educating and protecting customers on how their data is secured and used responsibly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Thirdly, requiring such firms to ensure adequate efforts and resources are devoted to educating and protecting customers in terms of how their data is secured and how it is being used responsibly, including in the digital eco-system.

sections.label: Bill aligns with FATF standards
sections.summary: The Bill provides compliance requirements for cryptocurrency businesses aligning legislation with FATF standards and expands DPT and cross-border money transfer definitions for MAS oversight.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The Bill provides clear compliance requirements for cryptocurrency businesses that will align our legislation with the enhanced standards adopted by the international Financial Action Task Force (FATF).

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The additional requirements are necessary to counter money laundering and terrorist financing risks associated with some virtual asset service providers which are not already regulated as financial institutions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The expanded definitions of digital payment token (DPT) service and cross-border money transfer service will also enable MAS to have a more comprehensive oversight.

sections.label: DPTs as collateral
sections.summary: The speaker asks MAS to assure that DPTs will not be used as collateral for working capital facilities to DPT holders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: They could potentially perform the functions of money and can be traded, too.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I seek MAS’ assurance that DPTs will not be allowed to be used as collateral to grant working capital facility to the DPT holders as this is one form of encashment.

sections.label: Bill increases DPT regulation
sections.summary: The Bill will bring about increased regulations and scrutiny over DPT.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The Bill will bring about increased regulations and scrutiny over DPT.

sections.label: Policing online crypto marketing
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether the Government will police online marketing of cryptocurrencies given increased scrutiny on DPT service providers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: With increased scrutiny on DPT service providers, will the Government police online marketing of cryptocurrencies?

sections.label: Mandatory customer verification exchanges
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether the Government would make it mandatory for all licensed crypto exchanges to require customers to be verified.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Would the Government make it mandatory for all licensed crypto exchanges to require customers to be verified?

sections.label: Equipping Home Team against crypto crime
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether the Government will equip the Home Team to combat cryptocurrency money laundering, frauds and scams.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Will the Government look into equipping our Home Team to prevent and combat not just cryptocurrency money laundering but also frauds and scams?

sections.label: Public education and digital payments
sections.summary: The Government will need to consider a public education campaign, and Asia's annual payments growth is 15% CAGR.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The Government will need to consider a public education campaign, so that everyone can benefit from the technology while avoiding the pitfalls.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: In Asia, the annual growth of payments is at 15% CAGR, fueled by the adoption and growth of alternative digital payments mechanisms with a strong push to reduce the use of cash.

sections.label: Payment revenues at customer end
sections.summary: Over 80% of total payment revenues are captured at the end of the value chain where the customer relationship is.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: More than 80% of the total payment revenues are captured at the end of the value chain where the customer relationship is.

sections.label: Muted transaction fee growth
sections.summary: Transaction fee growth for payments has been muted over three years due to competitive pressures depressing margins, and added requirements pass regulatory and compliance costs to consumers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: Over the last three years, transaction fee growth for payments has been muted because of the competitive pressures that have continued to depress margins.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: This means that when additional requirements are implemented, additional regulatory and compliance cost will be passed on to the consumer, increasing business cost.

sections.label: Mainstream adoption of digital assets
sections.summary: Conventional asset managers hold Bitcoins, PayPal enables cryptocurrency funding, and DBS and SGX launched the DBS Digital Exchange in December 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Conventional asset managers such as Ruffer and MassMutual now have Bitcoins as part of their asset allocation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: PayPal is enabling cryptocurrency as a funding source for digital commerce and our very own DBS and SGX have launched the DBS Digital Exchange in December 2020 to welcome the mainstream adoption of digital assets and currency trading.

sections.label: Payment service provider application approvals
sections.summary: The Act came into force on 28 January 2020, but about 361 companies remain on the exemption list awaiting their PSA licence application outcome.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In keeping with the spirit of progress, we should also consider the progress made in assessing payment service provider applications and the pace at which approvals are given.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Now, I note that while the Act came into force on 28 January 2020, there remains about 361 companies that are still on the exemption list and awaiting the outcome of their PSA licence application.

sections.label: E-wallet holding and transaction limits
sections.summary: Under the current Payment Services Act, e-wallet users can hold no more than $5,000 and transact no more than $30,000 each year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Under the current Payment Services Act, e-wallet users can hold no more than $5,000 in their accounts while they can transact no more than $30,000 each year.

sections.label: Compensation and penalties for hacks
sections.summary: 2FA avoids account takeover through password theft, but customers remain vulnerable to inadequate systemic protection; the speaker asks how customers will be compensated and what penalties issued after a hack, and whether deposit insurance for digital payment and crypto providers is feasible.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: So, 2FA would avoid account takeover through password theft, but a customer is still vulnerable to inadequate systemic protection measures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: I wish to ask, under the amendments, if a hack is to occur and millions of funds are lost, how will customers be compensated and what penalties will be issued?

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Should we perhaps look into the feasibility of deposit insurance for providers of digital payments and crypto services?

sections.label: Penalties for data protection failures
sections.summary: Service providers who fail to protect consumer data must be penalised under the Personal Data Protection Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Service providers who failed to protect consumer's data must be penalised under the Personal Data Protection Act.

sections.label: Cross-exchange cryptocurrency market manipulation
sections.summary: Traders with large cryptocurrency amounts may manipulate markets across exchanges, which is difficult to detect despite anti-manipulation protocols.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Meanwhile, sophisticated traders who have purchased large amounts of cryptocurrency may manipulate the market across several exchanges in parallel.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Although reputable exchanges tend to be regulated with anti-manipulation protocols in place, manipulation across multiple exchanges is difficult to detect.

sections.label: MAS response to advisers
sections.summary: The question asks what MAS' response is to Singapore advisers wanting to include these products in clients' portfolios.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: My question is, what is MAS' response to advisers in Singapore who want to include these products in their clients' portfolios?

sections.label: Token issuance licensing and process
sections.summary: The passage asks whether token issuers need a licence under new amendments and how long or complex the process is.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: A more stable and well-regulated fintech industry will be a boost for technology start-ups particularly for those who wish to get funding via Initial Coin Offerings or ICO.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: I wish to clarify whether under the new amendments, would issuers of tokens require a licence?

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: How long or complex is the typical process for a company to get into the business of issuing tokens?

sections.label: Payment Services Act licence architecture
sections.summary: The passage states the Payment Services Act has different licence classes, a differentiated approach and a risk-based approach.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: When we passed this Bill, I did so in January 2019, and we explained this.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: It is fundamentally the entire architecture of the Payment Services Act to have different classes of licences, differentiated approach and adopt the principle of taking a risk-based approach.

sections.label: AML/CFT rules for DPT providers
sections.summary: MAS imposes stringent AML/CFT requirements on licensed DPT service providers, including know-your-customer measures in line with FATF standards.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: For financial transactions, where there are real concerns of money laundering or terrorism financing, it is all the more necessary to have regulations that require the keeping of data and records.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Hence, MAS imposes stringent AML/CFT requirements on licensed DPT service providers in Singapore to mitigate against the risks of abuse of our financial centre by bad actors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: In line with the Financial Action Task Force or FATF standards, DPT service providers must conduct know-your-customer measures for this purpose.

sections.label: International DPT legislation comparisons
sections.summary: The speaker says Singapore keeps abreast of international developments and that the US, Japan, Australia, Switzerland and several EU members have passed similar DPT legislation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: We are active in this space internationally and we keep abreast of the developments and certainly not running ahead of international best practices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: So, whatever the legislation we are proposing, US, Japan, Australia, Switzerland, several EU members have already passed similar legislation to regulate their DPT service providers.

sections.label: MAS stablecoin consultation paper
sections.summary: MAS has issued a consultation paper to review whether further changes are needed to address risks associated with stablecoins.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: MAS has therefore issued a consultation paper to review if further changes are needed to address risks associated with stablecoins.

sections.label: DPT customer data requirements
sections.summary: The Bill's amendments will allow MAS to impose additional requirements on DPT service providers to protect customers' data.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: The amendments under the Bill will allow MAS to impose additional requirements on DPT service providers to protect customers' data, precisely for the reasons raised by Members.

sections.label: Fines for cyber hygiene breaches
sections.summary: An entity found to have breached MAS' cyber hygiene requirements can be fined up to $100,000 on conviction.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Further, if the entity is found to have breached MAS’ cyber hygiene requirements, it can be subject to fines of up to $100,000 on conviction.

sections.label: CAD blocking DPT advertisements
sections.summary: The CAD has to-date removed or blocked more than 150 advertisements and websites promoting suspicious investments involving DPTs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: The CAD has also, to-date, removed or blocked more than 150 advertisements and websites promoting suspicious investments featuring or involving DPTs.

sections.label: Payment Services Act user protection
sections.summary: The amendments introduce additional user protection powers in the Payment Services Act, but laws cannot protect against investment losses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Today’s amendments introduce additional user protection powers in the Payment Services Act, but it is not possible for laws to protect against investment losses.

sections.label: DPT disclosure and licensing
sections.summary: MAS requires licensed DPT providers to disclose risks, correct misleading statements, and licence entities facilitating DPT transactions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: MAS requires licensed DPT service providers to clearly disclose to their customers that they should buy DPTs only if they are familiar with the product and are prepared to accept the risk of losing all the money put into the DPTs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: If DPT service providers make a statement that suggests that investment in DPT is protected under the Payment Services Act, MAS will require them to immediately correct or remove the statement, and they will be subject to enforcement actions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: In response to Mr Saktiandi’s question, any entity which facilitates DPT transactions as described in the Payment Services Act today or in the amendments under today’s Bill, including persons facilitating transactions, will be required to obtain a licence.

sections.label: Digital token issuers raising capital
sections.summary: Issuers using digital tokens to raise public capital face full securities issuance requirements, including issuing a prospectus.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Where the digital tokens are used by issuers as a way to raise capital from the public, the issuers will be subject to the full set of regulatory requirements applicable for securities issuance, such as the need to issue a prospectus.

sections.label: DPT consumer protection safeguards
sections.summary: The Bill gives MAS powers to require DPT service providers to put in place consumer protection safeguards.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: We should use alternate means in our regulatory toolbox to deal with risks associated with DPT, which is what the Payment Services Act seeks to do.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: That is why the Payment Services (Amendment) Bill today provides MAS the powers to require DPT service providers to put in place consumer protection safeguards.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Today, under the Payment Services Act, major payment institutions are required to safeguard customer monies by depositing them in a separate trust account, or obtaining either an undertaking or guarantee from a bank in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: With the provisions made, MAS will review the need to impose safeguarding measures on DPT service providers.

sections.label: Moneychangers transition and licence requests
sections.summary: Existing players including moneychangers get a six to 12 months' grace period, and MAS will consider extension requests case-by-case.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Also, they are affected by technology, as there are now alternatives to remittances.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: We have a six to 12 months' grace period for existing players to transit into the new regulatory framework, so this applies also to moneychangers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Several moneychangers have made requests to MAS to temporarily cease their licences due to poor business.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Several requested for further extensions beyond the six months and MAS will consider their request on a case-by-case basis.

sections.label: MAS applications received
sections.summary: MAS has received over 300 applications so far.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: MAS has received over 300 applications so far.
